name: Tea Green
lede: Tea Green is a pale, fresh green named in dictionaries for the greyish green of green tea, though the swatch is much lighter than the leaf.

sections.title: The color of green tea
sections.body:
Paterson defines tea green as the greyish green of green tea [1]. The swatch here is a pale, light green with little grey in it; it sits 8.0 units from [[mint]] [2]. So the name points to a duller color than the screen shows, and people now use it for the pale tint.

The name is old for a color word of this kind. Maerz and Paul, whose 1930 dictionary our library cites, date it to 1858 [2]. It also appears on Ridgway's 1912 color atlas and in the ISCC-NBS list of 1955, block 122 [2]. Related pale greens in our data include [[celadon]] and [[light-green]]. Who first used it for this color is undocumented.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color near this swatch appears in only 8 of 23,781 paintings in our archive, 0.03 per cent, rarer than 75 per cent of named colors [3]. The earliest dated match is 1867, in a painting by Charles de Tournemine, 45 years before Ridgway's atlas [3]. With so few cases, and these being photographs of aged paintings, no pattern is safe to draw.
